_purpose: GAP-2026-08-15-PYQCOUNT-DRIVE-ACQUISITION, patch P7 — the class-level fix. A remediation that establishes a LAW must be applied to EVERY spec the law governs, and the completeness of that application must be MACHINE-CHECKABLE. GAP-2026-07-26-003 was remediated file-by-file from a changelog list; the PYQ counting path was not on that list; five days later a file split copied the unfixed text forward 'content byte-identical' into a file that never mentions the GAP id. A law enforced by a checklist is a law that will be re-broken by the next file split.
_enforced_by: audit_sync.py. This file is DATA, not documentation: audit_sync hard-fails if it is missing, malformed, or out of step with the corpus.
_derived_not_declared: The 'governs' list is CHECKED AGAINST THE CORPUS, never trusted. Any spec that performs a governed operation but is absent from 'governs' is a FAIL — that is the half a hand-maintained list can never provide, and it is the half that failed in July. Adding a spec to 'governs' does not exempt it from anything; it subscribes it to 'verified_by'.
_on_file_split: Any file split MUST re-run audit_sync against BOTH halves before the split is committed. The 2026-07-31 PYQAnalyse v2.29 -> PYQCount v1.0 split is precisely how this defect entered production.

EXECUTION-BOUNDARY-LAW.requires: A tool call cannot happen inside a running python process. Every spec performing a CLASS T operation must declare it as a tagged pass-bodied stub AND inject a RESOLVER over already-materialised results at every injection point. Never inject the CLASS T marker name itself, and never inject a name the spec does not bind.
EXECUTION-BOUNDARY-LAW.detect_note: A spec PERFORMS this operation when its text contains a live (non-comment) call to a documented injection point — audit_callgraph.INJECTION_POINTS. Commented-out historical examples do not count; a spec is expected to quote the defect it fixed.
preconditions: INSPECTABILITY. No 'CLASS: T' or 'CLASS: J' marker may appear inside a fence that fails ast.parse. audit_callgraph.any_python_blocks() yields only compiling fences BY DESIGN, so a marker in a non-compiling fence is — to C6 — a stub that does not exist: C6 builds an empty class_t set, returns early, and never scans the consumption sites, which compile fine one fence away. The law then reports 0 findings on a file it cannot verify. Measured 2026-08-15 on Framework_MockTestAnalyse.md: untagged fence 321-603 failed ast.parse at line 328 on an em-dash IN PROSE; both gdrive stubs lived in it; two live violations at lines 655 and 658 went unreported while four auditors were green. Enforced by audit_callgraph:C6-PRE. A check that can be structurally disarmed by the shape of its input is not a check; it is a check-shaped hole.

PRODUCER. A resolver injected at a documented injection point must read a container that something in the same spec actually FILLS — an assignment in compiling python, a parameter with no default, or a defaulted parameter whose absence raises. A bare default of None or {} is not a producer; it is the defect. C6 checks 'declared and passed', C7 checks 'not declared and passed', and neither can see a correct injection over an empty container. Enforced by audit_callgraph:C9.

_on_partial_remediation: A GAP remediated in one governed spec MUST be re-verified against EVERY spec in 'governs' before the GAP is closed, and the re-verification must be the CI RUN, not a reading. GAP-2026-08-15-PYQCOUNT-DRIVE-ACQUISITION was closed after fixing Step 4; Step 5 was described in its own changelog as 'the reference implementation' and never re-read against the new contract; Step 5's Drive lane was dead the whole time, could silently emit a deliverable of zero-PYQ scaffolds, and four auditors reported 0 findings. 'Already correct' must mean 're-verified against the new contract', never 'not the file the defect was reported in'.
